Meeting header:

Auto-summary (auto-generated):
- Primary ask: Understand Redwood options (Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private) for Horizon's low-latency chat endpoints and multi-region failover strategy.
- Key constraints: strict EU data residency for subset of traffic, 99.95% write-path SLA target, 100ms p95 for US region, incremental budget constraints.
- Immediate follow-ups: Redwood to provide SLA matrix and warm-pool sizing, Horizon to send traffic histograms.

Topics covered:
- current architecture and pain points
- multi-region routing and health detection
- fallback policies (model variant fallbacks, fanout, graceful degradation)
- latency vs cost tradeoffs; warm pools and KV/prefix cache priming
- security, KMS and SOC2/ISO questions

Transcript body:
[00:00] Maya (Redwood AE): Hey everyone, thanks for joining. quick intro from us — I'm Maya, AE, and Diego will handle the technical stuff. how about you all?
[00:08] Aisha (Horizon): Hi, Aisha here. Head of platform. Marcus is our SRE lead, Priya on security, Jonah product. thanks for taking the time.
[00:15] Diego (Redwood SE): great to meet you. I'd like to get a sense of your traffic patterns and what "fallover" means for you operationally. is it full region failover or partial degrade?
[00:26] Marcus (Horizon): Mostly partial. we have chat and routing endpoints; chat must stay up for premium customers, but for free tier we can degrade. We aim for 99.95% overall, but per-tenant SLOs differ.
[00:36] Jonah (Horizon): also, our EU customers need data to stay in eu-west region for regulatory reasons — that's non-negotiable for a subset of traffic.
[00:45] Maya (Redwood AE): great — that points to a mixed strategy. we can discuss Hosted with region restrictions, Dedicated reserved pools per region, or Private for full control. Diego, maybe you walk through options quickly?
[00:56] Diego (Redwood SE): sure. so, three modes at a high level: Hosted (fastest onboarding, multi-region but less customer-managed), Dedicated (reserved GPU pools you control via config, predictable throughput), Private (VPC or on-prem where control and residency are yours). in terms of failover, we support policy-based routing: prefer-region, failover-to-compatible-model, and partial-degrade where we route to cheaper smaller model or return cached responses.
[01:24] Priya (Horizon): quick Q — in hosted, is there tenant-level data separation? our compliance folks worry about co-mingled logs and key access.
[01:33] Maya (Redwood AE): Hosted is logically isolated and encrypted in transit and at rest; we have KMS integrations but for strict compliance Private or Dedicated with VPC peering is recommended. we do offer audit logs, though for SOC2/ISO attestation you'll want Dedicated or Private typically.
[01:46] Marcus (Horizon): okay. for failover detection, what do you use? dns, healthchecks, or application-level hooks? we need sub-10s fail detection ideally for hot paths.
[01:56] Diego (Redwood SE): we use a mix. active health probes + passive error-rate detection + circuit breakers in the routing plane. detection windows are configurable — default is 30s but can be tuned down; we also support traffic mirroring and staged cutovers for canaries. note lower detection windows may increase false positives under transient network blips.
[02:18] Jonah (Horizon): how about model fallbacks — if we lose the big LLM, can you auto-fallback to a smaller quantized variant? what's the latency impact?
[02:27] Diego (Redwood SE): yes. we have model variant family mapping. fallback to a smaller quantized model usually reduces throughput cost and latency, but quality may drop. p95 latency for a fallback path depends on sequence length; as a rough number, in our infra a medium quantized 13B model on Dedicated can do ~120ms p95 for typical chat sequences, larger models are higher. We'll need your payload sizes for a precise estimate.
[02:49] Priya (Horizon): KMS question — for Dedicated, can we use our existing KMS/HSM? we need to ensure key material never leaves our account.
[02:57] Maya (Redwood AE): yes, Dedicated supports customer-managed keys via KMS and for Private we support HSM integrations. we'll surface the exact flow in the security docs we send.
[03:08] Aisha (Horizon): on routing, we have an edge layer in front of your endpoints. is there a recommended split between client-side routing vs Redwood routing? we prefer making decisions in our edge if possible.
[03:18] Diego (Redwood SE): if you control edge routing, that's fine. we provide route policies and region tags and a traffic steering API. typical pattern: client-edge chooses preferred region; if error or elevated latency then send to Redwood region with failover tag; Redwood routing can also do automatic steering if you give us a global view.
[03:36] Marcus (Horizon): what's the recommendation for warm pools and KV cache priming? we've seen cold-starts on kv cache hurt tail latency.
[03:45] Diego (Redwood SE): we recommend a small warm-pool sized to your peak concurrency plus a prefix-level KV cache priming for frequent prompts; Redwood Optimize can suggest batch sizes and cache TTLs. warm-pools keep a fraction of GPU workers hot; there is a cost tradeoff — warm pools cost reserved vCPU/GPU time. we can model cost vs tail latency for you.
[04:07] Jonah (Horizon): do you support graceful degradation responses? like returning a cached summary with an explanation when model path fails?
[04:14] Diego (Redwood SE): yes, you can configure structured fallback responses or use a rule that returns the latest cached response or a canned message. that's often used for non-critical flows.
[04:23] Aisha (Horizon): let's talk SLA wording — our procurement insists on 99.95% per-region and credits for both regional and cross-region failures. what's typical?
[04:33] Maya (Redwood AE): Hosted SLAs vary by tier; Dedicated comes with better uptime commitments. standard Dedicated SLA is 99.95% regional availability for the serving layer; for Private we negotiate. we'll send the SLA matrix. note that failover scenarios that are customer-configured (e.g., routing policy misconfig) are often excluded from SLA.
[04:55] Priya (Horizon): do you have runbooks for incident containment? can you integrate into our PagerDuty?
[05:01] Diego (Redwood SE): yes, we provide webhooks and alerting hooks, you can integrate directly with PagerDuty. we also supply runbook templates for common failure modes (GPU OOM, model load failures, region outage).
[05:14] Marcus (Horizon): performance test: we want to run a chaos sim with a regional blackout and see traffic steering and fallback quality. is that something Redwood supports in a pilot?
[05:23] Maya (Redwood AE): absolutely; we often run pilot chaos simulations with customers. typical cadence: pre-test baseline metrics, staged blackout, observe failover times, validate quality on fallback models. Diego will own the test plan with you.
[05:35] Diego (Redwood SE): yes, and we'll instrument the test with trace IDs, token-level latency breakdowns, and KV-hit rates so we can pinpoint where degradation happens.
[05:45] Aisha (Horizon): ok, on cost — if we use warm pools + dedicated regional capacity + fallback to quantized models for free-tier, what's the rough delta vs pure hosted?
[05:56] Maya (Redwood AE): depends a lot on volume but ballpark: dedicated reserved capacity ups the fixed costs but drops per-token cost and stabilizes latency. with warm pools you pay for reserved GPU time; if you need strong residency and predictable SLOs, Dedicated often ends up cheaper at scale for core traffic, Hosted better for spiky or low-volume. We'll quantify after we see your traffic histogram.
[06:17] Jonah (Horizon): security again — audit logs retention: Hosted retention is 90 days by default? we may need 1 year for some logs.
[06:25] Maya (Redwood AE): default hosted retention is 90 days; Dedicated can extend retention as an add-on; Private you fully control retention. We'll include retention options and pricing.
[06:36] Priya (Horizon): any concerns about token-level redaction and PII exposure with hosted? our legal asks for end-to-end redaction for certain endpoints.
[06:45] Diego (Redwood SE): we support pre-tokenization redaction hooks and client-side redaction best practices. we also support on-the-fly redaction rules in the routing plane for Hosted, but for the strictest guarantee Private is the option.
[06:59] Marcus (Horizon): what about multi-model fallbacks where we split traffic across models to reduce risk? can we have a mix: 70% primary, 30% fallback warm-pool?
[07:09] Diego (Redwood SE): yes — weighted routing and traffic-splits are supported for canaries and ongoing skew. you can do percentage-based routing with warm-pools for the fallbacks.
[07:19] Aisha (Horizon): let's put some specifics on timelines and pilot scope. goal: 2-week pilot for Hosted with simulated failovers, then evaluate Dedicated pilot. does that sound realistic?
[07:28] Maya (Redwood AE): that sounds good. proposed next steps: you send traffic histograms, we propose pilot config (warm-pool size, model variants, routing policies), run chaos sim, measure p95/p99 and failover time.
[07:39] Jonah (Horizon): Curious — are there any gotchas around model quantization and degradation of certain prompt patterns? we've seen hallucination rates spike on smaller models.
[07:48] Diego (Redwood SE): yes, quantization can affect certain instruction-following behaviors. we recommend pre-flight evals on a representative prompt set; Redwood Optimize can surface deltas and suggest prompt tuning or light re-ranking.
[07:59] Priya (Horizon): procurement note: if we go Dedicated, we need a contractual clause for geo-specific downtime credits. can you provide sample language?
[08:07] Maya (Redwood AE): yes, we'll include sample SLA language. we usually show regional SLA credits as percentage-based penalties for downtime windows.
[08:16] Marcus (Horizon): on observability, can you give token-level breakdowns per request and correlate with our traces? we want to find if latency is from model compute or network.
[08:26] Diego (Redwood SE): we provide token-level timing and per-stage breakdowns and support trace correlation via headers. we can also emit traces to your datadog or prometheus endpoint.
[08:36] Aisha (Horizon): any limitations for on-prem private deployments regarding GPU types? we standardize on A100s but some DCs have H100s.
[08:45] Diego (Redwood SE): Private supports a range of GPUs; we surface a compatibility matrix. kernel selection and compilation differ by architecture but our runtime has profiles for both A100 and H100. some models get better throughput on one vs the other; we'll include benchmark notes.
[08:59] Jonah (Horizon): what's the effort to get a dedicated regional pool up? weeks or months?
[09:05] Maya (Redwood AE): typically 2-6 weeks depending on contract, capacity availability, and networking (VPC peering, routing rules). Private on-prem is longer and needs security reviews.
[09:18] Priya (Horizon): for the pilot we'll probably push Hosted first to validate failover and fallback patterns before committing.
[09:24] Maya (Redwood AE): that's a pragmatic approach.
[09:26] Diego (Redwood SE): I'll draft a pilot config. can you also share the top 10 prompt templates and any eval sets you use? that will help us pick fallback models and quantify quality.
[09:37] Aisha (Horizon): yes we'll share prompt templates.
[09:40] Marcus (Horizon): one more thing — can Redwood throttle fallbacks to avoid overloading fallback model pool during region outage? we worry about thundering herd.
[09:50] Diego (Redwood SE): yes — the routing plane includes rate limiting and circuit-breakers; we can set global throttles and then ramp traffic to fallbacks gradually. we also support token-budget quotas per tenant so fallback cannot exhaust resources.
[10:03] Jonah (Horizon): ok wrapping up — recap?
[10:06] Maya (Redwood AE): recap: Horizon to send traffic histograms and prompt set; Redwood to send SLA matrix, cost delta, warm-pool sizing, and pilot plan. schedule tech deep dive for Private next week if needed.
[10:18] Priya (Horizon): timeline noted. Priya will prepare compliance questions.
[10:22] Maya (Redwood AE): perfect. we'll follow up with the docs and a calendar invite for pilot kickoff. thanks, everyone.
[10:29] Aisha (Horizon): thanks all.
[10:31] (call ends)
